findings.current: Esta app dirige las sesiones de tu propia máquina y muestra lo que hizo. Tu código nunca sale de ella.
findings.problem: The privacy claim's referent is ambiguous in Spanish: 'ella' can resolve to 'la app' (the sentence subject) or 'máquina'. The English context note fixes 'it' = the machine, and the promise must land on the machine. Same sentence shifts the source's 'on your machine' to 'de tu máquina'.
findings.suggestion: Esta app dirige las sesiones en tu propia máquina y muestra lo que hizo. Tu código nunca sale de tu máquina.

findings.current: …Radient gestiona el túnel por ti y te da una URL privada y autenticada…
findings.problem: One English verb, 'run a tunnel', is rendered 'gestiona' here and 'ejecutas' in the card directly below (paths.own_body: 'un túnel que ejecutas tú'), on the same choose-a-path screen. 'gestiona' also drops 'runs' and makes Radient a manager rather than the runner.
findings.suggestion: Requiere una cuenta de Radient. Radient ejecuta el túnel por ti y te da una URL privada y autenticada, así que no hay nada que configurar en este teléfono ni ninguna contraseña del relé que guardar.

findings.problem: 'ya' adds 'already', which the English does not say. Defensible as step-2 progress; the sentence stays grammatical around the untranslated {status} either way.

findings.current: Usar mi propio túnel en su lugar
findings.problem: Trailing 'en su lugar' keeps the English 'instead' word order and reads stiff on a quiet text button; 'su' has no clean antecedent. Length constraint is real (own_action already reads 'Usar mi propio túnel'), so this is a nit, not a defect.
findings.suggestion: Usar mi propio túnel en vez de Radient

findings.problem: Momentary noun reading 'route list' (la lista) in a badge that otherwise holds bare adjectives. The English forces the noun ('route ready') and the sibling badges are feminine adjectives, so the wording is right; noted for the record only.

findings.current: La quita de la lista de este teléfono. No afecta a la máquina, a su túnel ni a tu cuenta.
findings.problem: Sentence-initial 'La' is briefly ambiguous between article and object pronoun, and 'quita' between noun and verb. Both readings carry the same meaning, so no harm is done; an explicit subject removes the double take.
findings.suggestion: Esto la quita de la lista de este teléfono. No afecta a la máquina, a su túnel ni a tu cuenta.

findings.current: …publicas tu máquina por tu cuenta, con un túnel que ejecutas tú… y la contraseña la guardas tú.
findings.problem: Three first-and-second-person emphases in two sentences is heavier in neutral Spanish than in English, though the source does carry all three ('yourself', 'you run', 'you keep').
findings.suggestion: keep; if the card is tight, drop the last emphasis: '…y tú guardas la contraseña.'
